caption: Kar. 36. Altar (?)
reading: w?osi : sori(2)yi : tw?mklk[.](3)doye : aw?i?ḫ?loye tdḫe(4)lowi yi mkli (5)te[.][.]i?kelowi (6)tm?lñmk(7)sel?qo kdye (8)tdḫelowi mkso(9)r?mloli te(10)rikelowi (11)are(12)qeb?t?r (13)kditowi ato m(14)ḫe piso(15)ẖte at mḫe (16)pisiwekte (17)ḫmlolili pisi(18)tḫkte mklẖ(19)li
notes: Badly damaged, many hatched signs. Line 1: first sign of wosi hatched (w?); in soreyi the sign after r is drawn like i (4-shape), not S, so 'sori?yi' (formula expects e). Name in line 1-3 very uncertain: a dotted outline after the first hatched sign counted as one [.]; '3J' with a long tail read s? n?; the '/'+hooked sign after (3) read n? (could be d + o). Small s-shapes read l and large S read e by the table, but in -lowi the order was taken from the formula (ḫe-lowi, ke-lowi). Signs like a small hook with a long lower-left tail read t (table t), also possible l. 'Z with long flat tail' read k (as in kete); p is the Sigma-topped form. Line 13 'kd?i : ḫwi' unclear. Benedictions: 'ato mḫe piq?ẖ?te?' ('13'-like sign read q, could be s+i), 'at mḫe pisiw?ekte' (8-shaped sign is w by the table), 'ḫmlolili ... pisiẖḫkte'. Line 19 group 'm?k?e?ẖ?li' unclear.
check_notes: All 32 entries placed. Names table (deceased tw(?)mklk[.]doye, mother aw(?)i(?)ḫ(?)loye, father yimkli; second person tmlñmksel(?)qo, kdye, mksor(?)mloli), Index titles areqebr kditowi, Index C mklẖli (line 18-19), formulae A, B, C/D2 all found. Kept against type: mḫe in formula A (copy has C = ḫ, type 3 = ẖ); copy has one more sign (cross-shaped, read t?) between b and r of areqebr; copy has no divider before pisoẖte where the table prints one; copy leaves a gap inside yimkli. Hatching between m and l of mksormloli and between the two words of formula C dropped as damage, since the type has no sign there. ḫ?, i?, w? and r?, l? kept where Griffith prints (?).

notes: te is read for '/' + barred hook ('/+'), as in tedḫelowi. Line 1 name: '+' after '/' read te, 8 hatched (w?), then i d l; 'B'-like sign before the last strokes read q? (could be s), last strokes (sic) read y?. Line 2: sign after a is a 3 with long tail (ẖ?), a hatched sign, then a Z-like sign (k?). Line 6: the sic sign before rikelowi is a star/x shape, read te? from the formula. Line 6 'dse(7)a': loop sign d, 'V//' se, S+2 a. 'lobkwi': '/'+small s may be te. The 3-with-dot under sic in line 12 read to. Line 13: two n-like signs ('/^' with long tail), the first marked sic. Benedictions: 3-shaped sign in mẖe could be ḫ (formula mḫe); 'ν' before ḫ read b? (table b), its value unclear; '<' read ḫ. Line 16 begins with a sic sign (7 + reversed c) where a is expected: read a?. Line 17 last te has a dot under it (te? or to?). Many 3-shapes (m/ẖ/s) uncertain.
check_notes: All 38 entries placed. The check showed how this copy writes qo: a 3 or J followed by one stroke is q, the next stroke o (tewideqowi, ksyeqowi, msemeteyiqowi, meqometeli, qoreñ). The two strokes marked sic at the end of tewideqowi stand where the type has i (kept as i?). 'S + long-tailed 2' read a in step 1 is k + e (dseke, mleke). Kept against type: a hatched sign before psiẖebḫte that the type does not count. Index C has ẖolbḫte/ḫlml, formula D table ḫlẖl: the same printed J glyph; copy shows a closed 3, kept as ẖ?. mstowi: copy's to is marked sic by Griffith.

notes: No divider between wosi and soreyi in line 1. Line 2 'mesyñ?': Griffith prints '?' over the crossed sign. 'teri(4)kelo :' ends with lo (no wi in the copy). 'ml?l?a': two small s-shapes between m and a (cf. Kar. 37 line 12). The loop sign in my(5)reñ? may be d. 'simeotelowi': the '/' on both sides of the barred hook; left one taken as part of te. A second invocation wosi : soreyi starts line 6. In 'ato mẖ?e' the middle sign is a 3 (formula has ḫ). 'q?' in line 10 is '/3' (q, or o + s).
check_notes: All 27 entries placed. Index A types the place word as wimlotelowi, but the type shows a closed 3 (s), as in Index B and C (simlotelowi) and in the copy: recorded as a typing correction. ñ? kept: Griffith prints (?) over it. Index C simlotelo(wi) brackets wi; the copy shows wi.

notes: Double altar: the two texts (a, b) are copied in interleaved lines, each with its own line numbers. a line 3 name: crossed sign with a long base line read ñ?; dot + hook read t; 'V//' se; a 3 with a tick read m?; the text ends in five thin strokes (damage) written [.][.]. In 'psi?ẖ?te' the middle sign is a nu-like sign with a dot, read i? by comparison with Kar. 38 pisiẖte. The 3 in mẖe could be ḫ. Line 8: five thin strokes (damage) between m and l written [.][.]. 'q' = '/3'.
check_notes: Placed: names table 29/39 A (arilñmkseqo[wi]), Index C arilñmẖseqowi, formulae A, B, C for part a (and the unparted Index entries). The sign after m: names table and Index C print the same flat-Z glyph, typed k and ẖ; the copy has a plain 3; kept k?. The lost end [.][.] matches Griffith's [wi]. Copy keeps a divider between ḫmlol and ẖolkete that the table does not print.
